images.title: Pull back to the resource neighborhood
images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create the next Board atlas design frame from these two references. Image 1 is the preferred quiet material and shared ground layout; image 2 supplies resource building forms. The user likes the subtle fabric and spaciousness. This frame explores gently ZOOMING OUT to a resource neighborhood in an automatic emphasis mode, not switching to a separate world.
Preserve the relative world positions and separate identities of exactly three resources R17/R18/R19 and exactly three processes PID41/PID52/PID63. Pull the camera back about 15 percent, keeping the same orientation and R17 near the center-left. Leave ample white space. R17 has two connected Table wings labeled T1/T2 on ONE shared plot; R18 is modular KV; R19 is a stepped Document. Buildings rise from neutral ground. The process sites become small flat circular identity anchors. No raised process wells in this RESOURCE emphasis. The underlying ivory material remains gently textured and quiet, never mountainous.
Keep one selected dark-teal perimeter around R17 and the same three dashed association paths to it. No process moves inside a building, no extra objects and no literal city scenery.
Keep the existing slim Board header, scope Atlas / A.01 and search field. The top-right view switch is now "Canvas" selected and "Browse" unselected, because this study extends the canvas into resource interiors. Top-left canvas population remains "3 resources · 3 processes", with "Synthetic · complete".
Keep the exact compact R17 inspector at top right: "Resource R17", "2 Tables · shared resource", "Current values 32 MiB", "Writer PID 41", "Lifetime Independent", "3 visible associations". Change its main action label to "Enter resource". No other inspector or sidebar.
Replace the bottom-left legend's segmented switch with a SINGLE compact dropdown label "Auto · Resources" plus a small chevron. Below: "Current value bytes" and "Height: compressed · Footprint: layout". This control can later pin an emphasis; do not show its expanded menu. Retain bottom-right zoom/reset/Evidence controls and footer "Concept · synthetic data".
The scene must feel like the SAME quiet neighborhood seen from a little farther away. No tunnel, moving buildings, glowing portal, arrows painted over the UI, extra charts or decorative metrics. High-fidelity desktop screenshot, 16:9 landscape.

images.title: Enter the building as a flat data room
images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Edit this overhead Board resource detail into the FIRST FRAME INSIDE Resource R17, a proposed flat data workspace. Keep the warm ivory, subtle architectural outline, spacious screen, dark slate typography, restrained teal selection and slim Board header. High-fidelity 16:9 desktop screenshot.
The building does not become a photoreal room: its selected footprint expands into a calm overhead FLOOR PLAN of its two logical Tables. No perspective walls, furniture, windows, people, underground floors or physical storage claims. The two existing wings become two large separated flat rounded rectangular work areas, T1 on the left and T2 on the right, inside one subtle R17 outer perimeter. Their area does NOT encode bytes or rows.
Header breadcrumb changes to "Atlas / A.01 / R17". Keep the search field but placeholder becomes "Find a table or field". Top right has "Canvas" selected, "Browse" unselected.
Immediately below the header show one small back link "← Neighborhood". Beside it, one quiet status "Resource workspace · Synthetic". Remove the population line, the external PID circles and all dashed association lines. Those processes remain OUTSIDE the resource; no process is a child room.
Remove the entire floating R17 inspector and the bottom-left emphasis/height legend. Resource facts remain accessible through a small "Resource info" button at lower right next to zoom/reset; do not duplicate its byte count here. Keep an Evidence button and footer "Concept · synthetic data".
Within the left room, give a crisp title "T1" with smaller "Table". Beneath, one compact schema list: "sample_id  int64", "group_id  int64", "value  int64". These are declared synthetic fields. Under the list a small caption "Sample S1 · 6 rows" and ONE teal button "Explore sample".
Within the right room, give the title "T2" and smaller "Table"; below use only "Schema not loaded" and a quiet "Inspect metadata" text button. Do not invent its columns or data.
Both room identities stay legible; T1 has a restrained teal inner outline to show it is selected. The outer site is one resource, not a nesting of processes. Plenty of breathing room, no dense grid, no extra panes, no fake data visualization yet. The entry action itself has NOT run a query; this is a source/structure selection workspace.

images.title: A visual worksheet for one bounded sample query
images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Use the input image as the exact visual material, typography and application-frame reference for a proposed Board data workspace. Make a flat spacious VISUAL QUERY WORKSHEET inside R17's Table T1. High fidelity desktop, 16:9. Ivory background, subtle shadows, crisp readable slate typography and dark teal accents. No 3D landforms or architecture remain at this reading distance.
Keep the slim Board header. Breadcrumb "Atlas / A.01 / R17 / T1". Search placeholder "Find a field". Top-right switch "Canvas" selected and "Browse" unselected. Below header, small "← Resource R17" back link at left, "Q1 · Synthetic sample" in the middle, and one teal "Run query" button at right. A small status beneath reads "Sample S1 · Complete for sample". This is explicitly a six-row sample, not the full Table or the resource byte total.
Lay out THREE large flat cards across the broad canvas with generous gaps and simple thin directional connectors left to right. They are query dependencies, not process associations. No executable code, SQL, joins, pipelines to external services, or application business meanings.
Left card: title "Source · T1"; subtitle "Sample S1 · 6 rows"; three field rows "sample_id  int64", "group_id  int64", "value  int64".
Middle card: title "Filter"; a clean editable-looking condition "group_id = 2". One small caption "Applied to sample S1".
Right card, slightly wider: title "Result Q1"; subtitle "3 matching sample rows". A crisp minimal table with EXACT columns "sample_id", "group_id", "value" and EXACT three rows:
102 | 2 | 13
104 | 2 | 34
105 | 2 | 55
Use enough width to keep all headers/values legible. Beneath the result table, one short line "Source: T1 · Sample S1". Do not repeat a total or create a chart.
The result is already completed in this synthetic illustration; Run query is an explicit rerun action, switching Canvas/Browse does not run it. Keep one unobtrusive bottom-left label "Query steps" with a tiny right-arrow key, bottom-right zoom/reset/Evidence controls, footer "Concept · synthetic data".
Avoid extra sidebars, dashboards, fake counters, colored status badges, building rooms around each query card, or a second copy of the result. This is a visual worksheet anchored to a resource, with a source, filter and actual readable bounded result.

images.title: Browse shows the same query and result

Select Browse in the top-right switch; Canvas becomes unselected.
Replace the three spatial query cards and connecting arrows with a calm conventional query form and a wide READ-ONLY result table. High-fidelity spacious desktop, 16:9; same ivory/slate/teal visual system.
One compact query form across the upper content area: a source dropdown labeled "Source" with "T1", a scope field labeled "Scope" with "Sample S1 · 6 rows", and a filter row labeled "Filter" with three form controls "group_id", "=", "2". Keep query structure simple. No SQL editor, invented query language, extra queries, joins, aggregate charts or save/export controls.
Below, give the result its own wide but restrained panel titled "Result Q1" with the subtitle "3 matching sample rows". A readable table with EXACT columns "sample_id", "group_id", "value", and EXACT rows:
102 | 2 | 13
104 | 2 | 34
105 | 2 | 55
Give rows comfortable spacing and align numeric cells. Show only these three rows, no implied pagination or large population count. Beneath, a small "Source: T1 · Sample S1" line.
No visible graph connectors or map controls remain in Browse. Retain a small Evidence button at lower right and footer "Concept · synthetic data". Preserve plenty of blank space below the finite result. This view is precise query composition and results inspection, not a spreadsheet editor. Numbers, source, query identity and sample coverage are unchanged from the input image.
